title: U.S. House · New York's 3rd Congressional District
area: Parts of northern/central Nassau County on Long Island (including the towns of North Hempstead, Oyster Bay, and the city of Glen Cove), plus a portion of northeast Queens.

context.text: This is a rematch of the 2024 general election, when Suozzi defeated LiPetri 51.7% to 48.1%. Both advanced from contested primaries on June 23, 2026: Suozzi defeated Danielle Welch 79.3% to 20.5% in the Democratic primary, and LiPetri defeated Gregory Hach 81.9% to 17.2% in the Republican primary.

The district voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election (51.4%–47.1%) while simultaneously electing Suozzi, a Democrat, to the House. As of July 21, 2026, The Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated the general election "Lean Democratic," and DDHQ/The Hill rated it "Likely Democratic." The NRCC named LiPetri to its MAGA Majority target-district program; the DCCC named Suozzi to its Frontline program for competitive incumbents.
NY-3 is the third-wealthiest congressional district in New York and was the thirteenth-wealthiest nationally as of 2024.

candidates.name: Tom Suozzi
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for NY-3 (since February 2024; also represented the district 2017–2023)

summary.text: Tom Suozzi is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 3rd Congressional District, having won a February 2024 special election and been re-elected that November. He previously represented the district from 2017 to 2023, and earlier served as Nassau County Executive (2002–2009) and Mayor of Glen Cove (1994–2001). He sits on the House Ways and Means Committee and co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus.

background.text: Earned a B.S. from Boston College (1984) and a J.D. from Fordham University (1989); worked as a certified public accountant and lawyer before entering politics.
Served as Mayor of Glen Cove, New York, from 1994 to 2001.
Served as Nassau County Executive from 2002 to 2009.
Represented NY-3 in the U.S. House from 2017 to 2023; returned to the seat by winning the February 13, 2024 special election over Mazi Pilip, then won the November 2024 general election over LiPetri.

priorities.text: Campaign centers on a five-point "American Affordability Plan": rolling back tariffs, phasing out U.S. involvement in the Iran war, paying down federal debt, expanding energy production, and making healthcare more affordable.

On tariffs: "Get rid of irresponsible tariffs that are driving up prices on groceries, cars, building materials, and everyday goods — while fighting for trade deals that bring manufacturing jobs back to America," citing his co-sponsorship of the Stop Global Tariffs Act.
priorities.quote: Get rid of irresponsible tariffs that are driving up prices on groceries, cars, building materials, and everyday goods — while fighting for trade deals that bring manufacturing jobs back to America.

priorities.text: On healthcare: says he will "protect and strengthen the tax credits that lower your health insurance premiums, invest in prevention and primary care, and pass the WISH Act to make long-term care more affordable so seniors can stay in their homes."
priorities.quote: Protect and strengthen the tax credits that lower your health insurance premiums, invest in prevention and primary care, and pass the WISH Act to make long-term care more affordable so seniors can stay in their homes.

priorities.text: On the federal debt: says he will "rein in federal spending so the government pays less in interest, reducing pressure on interest rates that affect mortgages, car loans, and credit card debt," citing the bipartisan Fiscal Stability Framework.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, co-sponsoring the Stop Global Tariffs Act to roll back presidential tariff authority and refund businesses that paid tariffs.
positions.quote: Get rid of irresponsible tariffs that are driving up prices on groceries, cars, building materials, and everyday goods.

positions.summary: Supports extending enhanced ACA premium tax credits (his bipartisan HOPE Act would extend them two years with fraud safeguards) and authored the WISH Act to make long-term care more affordable.

Has distanced himself from national Democrats on immigration, voting for the Laken Riley Act, while also introducing bipartisan legislation with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick to fund DHS and enact "targeted, enforceable reforms" to ICE.

record.text: Introduced the bipartisan Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act (H.R. 9187) with Rep. Tom Cole (R-OK) on June 15, 2026, to create an independent commission to address Social Security's long-term solvency; the bill was endorsed by the American Enterprise Institute, Third Way, Progressive Policy Institute, and National Taxpayers Union.

Introduced the bipartisan Supporting Newborn Parents Act of 2026 on May 14, 2026, with Reps. David Valadao (R-CA), Debbie Dingell (D-MI), and Blake Moore (R-UT), creating a newborn tax credit of up to $2,000 to help cover early childcare costs.
Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (2025–2026), including its Oversight and Tax subcommittees.
Co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus (25 Democrats and 25 Republicans); helped negotiate the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act according to his campaign.

Introduced the Reforming ICE and Protecting America Act with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), bipartisan legislation to fully fund the Department of Homeland Security for Fiscal Year 2026 while enacting reforms to ICE.

candidates.name: Michael LiPetri Jr.
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23 Republican primary; advanced from the Conservative Party primary, which was canceled
candidates.currentRole: Attorney; former New York State Assembly member, District 9 (2019–2021)

summary.text: Michael LiPetri Jr. is a Republican and Conservative Party candidate challenging Rep. Tom Suozzi in a rematch of their 2024 race. He represented New York State Assembly District 9 from 2019 to 2021 and is an attorney and former talk show host. He is endorsed by President Donald Trump.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in political science and government from the University at Albany and a J.D. from Albany Law School of Union University.
Professional experience includes working as an attorney and talk show host.

Represented New York State Assembly District 9 from 2019 to 2021; served on the Assembly's Corporations/Authorities/Commissions, Housing, Environmental Conservation, Racing and Wagering, and Social Services committees; did not seek re-election in 2020.
Lost the 2024 general election for NY-3 to Suozzi, 48.1% to 51.7%.

priorities.text: On affordability: "Affordability starts with letting Americans keep more of what they earn. That means building off the success of the Trump tax cuts - including lifting the SALT tax cap to protect New York families and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security."
priorities.quote: Affordability starts with letting Americans keep more of what they earn. That means building off the success of the Trump tax cuts - including lifting the SALT tax cap to protect New York families and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.

priorities.text: On law enforcement: says he was "the #1 supporter of Law Enforcement lauded by the Suffolk County PBA for being the only state legislator from Long Island to 100% Back The Blue," as a state assemblyman.
priorities.quote: During the height of the 'Defund the Police' movement, I was the #1 supporter of Law Enforcement lauded by the Suffolk County PBA for being the only state legislator from Long Island to 100% Back The Blue.

priorities.text: On his campaign message: says flipping the seat is about "stopping the Mamdani Madness and lawlessness from spreading to Long Island."
priorities.quote: Flipping this seat and stopping the Mamdani Madness and lawlessness from spreading to Long Island is critical.

positions.summary: Supports continued deportation of people in the country illegally and describes the U.S. immigration system as needing stricter enforcement of legal entry.
positions.quote: We must continue to deport those criminals here illegally and demand that every immigrant - like our parents and grandparents - enter this country legally and with pride.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a strong supporter of law enforcement funding and opposes the "Defund the Police" movement.
positions.quote: During the height of the 'Defund the Police' movement, I was the #1 supporter of Law Enforcement.

positions.summary: Opposes government/insurer control of healthcare decisions, favoring a system that emphasizes personal choice of doctors, portability, and price transparency over expanded public coverage.
positions.quote: We must restore the bond between patients and their doctors, not insurance companies and bureaucrats who wish to control the system.

positions.summary: Supports continued and forceful U.S. backing of Israel and opposes boycott/divestment/sanctions campaigns against it.
positions.quote: Any attempt to boycott, divest from, or sanction Israel must be shut down, eliminated, and swiftly dealt with.

positions.summary: Platform emphasizes parental control over education and family decisions generally, without a specific voucher or charter-school proposal documented.

record.text: As a New York State Assembly member (2019–2021), served on the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Housing; Environmental Conservation; Racing and Wagering; and Social Services committees.
Co-chaired a statewide Water Quality Taskforce as a State Assemblyman, according to his campaign, aimed at addressing aging water infrastructure and contamination.
Endorsed by President Donald Trump, U.S. Rep. Tom Emmer, Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, and the Nassau County Republican Party for the 2026 race.
